**STEP 2 - Ruler:** The white vessel is a small shallow bowl or paper plate, about 18 cm across. Area = 3.14 × (9)² ≈ 254 cm².

**STEP 3 - Items:** Whole almonds only. No oil or sauce is visible.

**STEP 4 - Area:** Almonds cover roughly 80% of the vessel (about 200 cm²), with a few gaps at the rim.

**STEP 5 - Volume:** The pile is about 1.5 cm deep on average, so 200 cm² × 1.5 cm ≈ 300 ml. Sizing from individual pieces is more reliable: each almond is about 2.5 × 1.6 × 0.9 cm, roughly 1.9 ml. I count about 55 visible almonds, so about 105 ml of visible almond volume. The pile hides more below the surface, so I take the bulk-density estimate of about 300 ml as the gross volume.

**STEP 6 - Grams:** Whole nuts have a bulk density of about 0.5–0.6 g/ml. Using the piece count (about 1.2 g per almond × ~55 visible, plus hidden pieces) gives roughly 70 g. This is the more defensible figure.

**STEP 7 - Energy:** Almonds are about 579 kcal/100 g. 70 g × 5.79 ≈ 405 kcal.

**STEP 8 - Sanity check:** A standard 28 g serving is about 165 kcal, so 70 g (about 2.5 servings) at roughly 400 kcal is plausible for a bowl this size.

Estimated total: about 70 g of almonds, about 400 kcal. This is an approximate visual estimate.
